page: Microsoft Azure E2a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with one physical core providing two vCPUs via multithreading at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting standard x86 extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions.

Resource allocation provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 54 GB of local SSD temporary storage and operates without dedicated hardware GPUs. In memory evaluations, the server achieves average scores in PassMark memory tests (2021.37) and handles read-only cached bandwidth at 128.75 GB/sec, alongside large-block uncached read and write speeds of 32.32 GB/sec and 22.49 GB/sec respectively.

Benchmark results highlight single-threaded compute as a relative operational strength, where the Geekbench single-core score reaches 1582.0 and single-threaded gzip compression performs at 26.15 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded capacity is constrained by the two-vCPU allocation, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1974.0, a PassMark CPU score of 3138.26, and lower throughput in parallel tasks like software compilation and static web serving (2.51 GB/sec). Database write operations on Redis scale to 2.04 million operations per second.

Given its high memory ratio paired with a modest dual-thread processor, the E2a_v4 provides a cost-efficient footprint for memory-demanding applications that do not require intense parallel processing. The configuration is suited for mid-sized in-memory caching layers, lightweight relational databases, background data buffering, and low-concurrency enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure E2a_v4 is a memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz across 2 vCPUs on a single physical core. Configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a high 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio supported by 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside 54 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Benchmark metrics demonstrate solid single-thread performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 1582.0 and balanced memory handling, though overall parallel execution is bounded by the dual-vCPU count, evidenced by a multi-core score of 1974.0 and 2.04 million Redis operations per second. The server does not feature GPU acceleration. This profile offers a cost-efficient deployment tier specifically suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads including caching layers, small databases, and lightweight backend services requiring dedicated memory capacity.
